transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I am constantly being watched and monitored by a group of people, and I need it to stop. I can see them tracking my movements wherever I go, and it's making me very concerned for my safety.
Aside from seeing them track you, do you ever hear voices of people talking when there is no one around, or hear them discussing you?
No, I don't hear any voices or sounds when no one is around. I just see them watching me and tracking my movements.
Have you recently experienced periods of feeling very down, depressed, or on the other hand, unusually energetic, high, or irritable?
No, I haven't experienced any of those extreme mood swings. My mood has been relatively normal, just a bit stressed because of the constant monitoring.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to think clearly, organize your thoughts, or find the motivation to do your daily activities?

No, my mind is completely clear and I have no issues organizing my thoughts or getting things done. My daily life and motivation are totally normal, except for the stress and distraction of dealing with this constant monitoring.
How long have you been experiencing this constant feeling of being watched and monitored?
It has been going on for about a year and eight months now. It started back then and has just been constant every single day since.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were Delusional Disorder and Schizophrenia. Based on the patient's report of experiencing these beliefs for 20 months without any auditory hallucinations, disorganized speech, disorganized behavior, or negative symptoms, and with daily functioning and motivation remaining entirely normal apart from the stress of the delusion, Schizophrenia is ruled out. This clinical picture is characteristic of Delusional Disorder.
